prompt: Explain how the power grid balances supply and demand.
hook: Electricity must be made the instant it is used.

card.oneLiner: The grid must match generation to demand in real time, and variable solar and wind need flexibility from storage, hydro and demand management.
keyPoints: Supply and demand are balanced second by second.
Solar and wind output varies with weather and time of day.
Storage, flexible plants and demand response provide balance.
Grid infrastructure must be strengthened for more renewables.

framework.name: Central Electricity Authority
framework.gloss: National planning and technical standards for the grid.

framework.name: Ministry of Power
framework.gloss: Policy for generation, transmission and distribution.

whatYouCanDo: Shift heavy appliance use to off-peak hours where incentives exist.
Understand that a green grid needs storage and wires, not just panels.
Follow grid and RE integration reports.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Grid operations are technical and region-specific.

prompt: Explain why solar has become India's fastest-growing power source.
hook: The sun now competes on price.

card.oneLiner: Falling costs and strong policy have made solar India's cheapest source of new electricity, driving record capacity additions.
keyPoints: Solar tariffs have fallen sharply through competitive auctions.
Utility-scale parks and rooftop systems are both growing.
Land, grid connection and storage are the main constraints.
Solar pairs an intermittent source with a variable grid.

framework.name: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
framework.gloss: National solar targets and support schemes.

whatYouCanDo: Check rooftop solar and net-metering options for your home.
Compare the levelised cost of solar with alternatives.
Recognise that daytime solar needs backup for evenings.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Costs and targets change over time.

sources.title: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy

prompt: Explain coal's role in India's energy mix and how the transition is managed.
hook: The transition is real, but gradual.

card.oneLiner: Coal still supplies most of India's electricity, and shifting to clean power means retiring or repurposing old plants while protecting reliability and livelihoods.
keyPoints: Coal remains the largest source of generation.
New capacity is dominated by renewables.
Old, polluting plants are candidates for retirement.
A just transition supports workers and communities.

framework.name: Central Electricity Authority
framework.gloss: Official data on installed capacity and generation.

framework.name: NITI Aayog
framework.gloss: Policy analysis on the shift away from coal.

whatYouCanDo: Distinguish capacity share from generation share.
Support retraining and economic diversification in coal regions.
Track plans for plant retirement and repurposing.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Transition timelines depend on policy and demand.

prompt: Explain energy efficiency and how labels and standards save power.
hook: The cheapest unit of energy is the one you do not use.

card.oneLiner: Appliance standards, star labels and efficiency schemes cut electricity demand and emissions at low cost.
keyPoints: Star labels rate appliances on energy use.
Standards remove the least efficient models from the market.
Efficiency schemes have scaled LED lighting widely.
Industry efficiency is driven by target-based schemes.

framework.name: Energy Conservation Act, 2001
framework.gloss: Legal basis for efficiency standards and labels.

framework.name: Bureau of Energy Efficiency
framework.gloss: Administers appliance standards and the PAT scheme.

whatYouCanDo: Use LED bulbs and efficient fans and ACs.
Service appliances so they run efficiently.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Savings depend on usage and sizing.

prompt: Explain battery storage and why it is key to clean power.
hook: Batteries turn sunshine into round-the-clock power.

card.oneLiner: Energy storage smooths variable solar and wind output and provides backup, and falling battery costs are unlocking it across India's grid.
keyPoints: Storage shifts daytime solar to evening demand.
Batteries and pumped hydro provide different durations.
Storage also helps the grid with frequency and backup.
Domestic manufacturing is being promoted.

framework.name: Central Electricity Authority
framework.gloss: Grid planning for energy storage systems.

framework.name: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
framework.gloss: Support for battery and hybrid projects.

whatYouCanDo: Understand storage as an enabler, not a competitor, to solar.
Support schemes that pair renewables with storage.
Follow battery manufacturing and recycling policy.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Technology and costs are changing quickly.
